Archaeologists use AI to discover 303 unknown geoglyphs near Nazca Lines
Newly discovered figures dating back to 200BCE nearly double the number of known geoglyphs at enigmatic site
The paper said while it “took nearly a century to discover a total of 430 figurative Nazca geoglyphs”, using an AI system covering the entire Nazca region it “took just six months to discover 303 new figurative geoglyphs”.

results.title: 140+ New Nazca Lines Discovered in Peru
results.content:
Using artificial technology, a team of scientists have found 143 new Nazca Lines, including glyphs of humans, animals, and abstract shapes etched in the Peruvian desert floor.
Since 2004, a team of Japanese scientists have identified over 140 new Nazca Lines etched into the deserts of southern Peru.
In regards to their age, researchers determined these geoglyphs date back between 100 BC and 300 AD.

results.title: AI uncovers hundreds of new Nazca geoglyphs in breakthrough discovery
results.content:
By using AI, the team has identified more than 300 new figures, a process that would have taken decades if done manually.
Despite their size, many of these Nazca lines went unnoticed, even after their rediscovery in the 20th century.
Out of over 1,300 potential finds, the team confirmed 303 new figurative geoglyphs and 42 geometric ones.
These geoglyphs, created between 200 B.C. and A.D.

results.content:
Archaeologists with the Yamagata University Institute discovered 168 new geoglyphs at the UNESCO World Heritage Site, almost doubling the previous known total of 190.
Of the 168 total new images, 163 measure around 10m across.

results.title: Why the Nasca lines are among Peru's greatest mysteries | National Geographic
results.content:
In total, there are over 800 straight lines, 300 geometric figures and 70 animal and plant designs, also called biomorphs.
Peruvian archaeologist Toribio Mejia Xesspe was the first to systematically study the lines in 1926.
The rocks which cover the desert have oxidized and weathered to a deep rust color, and when the top 12-15 inches of rock is removed, a light-colored, high contrasting sand is exposed.
